intent: Customer demands an immediate Direct Debit Guarantee refund of a £900 DD collection (3 Sep) she says duplicated her £1,000 rent standing order (1 Sep), plus cancellation of the Direct Debit.
summary: No same-day refund on chat: records show the £900 collection matched the 24 Aug advance notice (which warned to cancel the standing order), so no payment error is identified; refer the Guarantee claim to the DD indemnity team for assessment, not a verdict. Ask whether she set up/accepted the 20 Aug Harbour Lets mandate. Send the DD cancellation for her secure confirmation (nothing in flight; next due ~3 Oct). Log her dissatisfaction as a complaint. Reply with what is and is not confirmed; the £1,000 SO is her own instruction and stays active for 1 Oct unless she instructs.

facts.claim: A £1,000.00 standing order to HARROW & VALE RE HARBOUR LETS LTD CA (ref RENT 27 ELM RD) debited on 1 Sep 2026; it was set up by the customer in Feb 2025, is active and next due 1 Oct 2026.
A £900.00 Direct Debit to H&V COLLECT / HARBOUR LETS (ref HL-27ELM-0091) debited on 3 Sep 2026 under a mandate created 20 Aug 2026 via originator invite.

An advance notice dated 24 Aug 2026 to priya.desai@example.net stated £900.00 would be collected on or around 3 Sep then monthly, and advised cancelling any rent standing order before the first collection to avoid paying twice; the collection matched the notice.
The customer asserts she never agreed to £900, that her rent is £1,000, and demands an immediate Guarantee refund of £900 and cancellation of the Direct Debit; she rejects being given options.
The agent has acknowledged both payments but no refund, cancellation or complaint has been recorded as executed.
The session is an authenticated in-app personal banking chat matched to the internal account view for Priya Desai.

missing: Whether the customer set up/accepted the Harbour Lets Direct Debit invite on 20 Aug 2026 (authorised mandate with a disputed amount) or did not authorise the mandate at all
Whether she received the 24 Aug advance notice email
Whether she wants the £1,000 standing order kept for 1 Oct or cancelled (no instruction given)
The indemnity/disputes team's determination on whether a Guarantee error exists

steps.instruction: Do not process a same-day Direct Debit Guarantee refund of the £900 collected 3 Sep 2026 (HL-27ELM-0091) on the chat. Reason to record: the collection amount and date matched the originator's 24 Aug advance notice held by the bank, so no payment error is identified on record; the claim is being referred for assessment (s3) rather than refused.

rationale.explanation: The customer asserts an error, but the only recorded facts show collection matching the advance notice; the duplicate arose from the still-active customer standing order. A refund cannot be confirmed on chat without the indemnity assessment, and the bank should neither pay nor give a final refusal now.
rationale.criterion: Guarantee claims address errors in DD setup/collection; identify the error and route without promising a refund for every dispute, and do not issue an automatic eligibility verdict

steps.instruction: Ask Priya Desai one question: 'Did you set up or accept the Harbour Lets Direct Debit invite on 20 August 2026 (reference HL-27ELM-0091), or did you not authorise this Direct Debit at all?'

rationale.explanation: Her statement 'I never agreed to £900' is ambiguous between an unauthorised mandate and an amount dispute with the landlord; which it is determines the indemnity route and is not recoverable from supplied records.
rationale.criterion: Request the precise missing fact when a gap changes the decision

steps.instruction: Ask the Direct Debit indemnity/payment disputes team to register and assess a Direct Debit Guarantee claim for the £900.00 collected on 3 Sep 2026, originator H&V COLLECT / HARBOUR LETS, reference HL-27ELM-0091. Pass: mandate created 20 Aug 2026 via originator invite; advance notice sent 24 Aug 2026 for £900 on/around 3 Sep then monthly; collection matched notice; customer asserts she never agreed to £900 and her rent is £1,000; £1,000 standing order to the same landlord debited 1 Sep. Ask them to determine whether a Guarantee error exists and to record the outcome.

rationale.explanation: The customer has made an express Guarantee claim; the bank's records point against a collection error but the claim must be assessed by the team that handles indemnity claims, not decided on chat.
rationale.criterion: Keep the Guarantee claim separate from changing future instructions and route it to the applicable process

steps.target: Direct Debit indemnity / payment disputes team

steps.instruction: Send Priya Desai an in-app secure confirmation to cancel the Direct Debit mandate to H&V COLLECT / HARBOUR LETS, reference HL-27ELM-0091 (no collection currently in flight; next collection indicated on or around 3 Oct). The confirmation text must state that cancellation does not reverse the 3 Sep £900 collection, does not change rent owed to Harbour Lets, and does not alter the £1,000 standing order due 1 Oct.

rationale.explanation: The customer explicitly asked for the Direct Debit to be cancelled; the session is authenticated and the mandate is identified, so the change is sent for her confirmation without touching the standing order she has not asked to change.
rationale.criterion: Reuse supplied mandate state and require only the missing authorisation; cancelling an instruction does not establish reversal of a collected payment or end the contract

steps.instruction: Ask the complaints team to log a complaint from Priya Desai (personal current account) about the bank not refunding £900 immediately under the Direct Debit Guarantee. Scope: £1,000 SO 1 Sep and £900 DD 3 Sep to Harbour Lets; customer says the £900 amount is wrong and she never agreed to it; remedy sought: £900 refund today and DD cancellation. Chronology: mandate 20 Aug, notice 24 Aug, chat 4 Sep. Link to the indemnity assessment in s3.

rationale.explanation: The customer has expressed dissatisfaction and demanded redress and rejected the agent's explanation; recording it preserves her complaint rights independent of the refund decision.
rationale.criterion: Handle the complaint and the operational query as separate work; do not make registration conditional on accepting an outcome; promise only acknowledgements actually available

steps.instruction: Reply in chat: 'I can see both payments: £1,000 by your standing order on 1 September and £900 by Direct Debit to Harbour Lets on 3 September. The Direct Debit Guarantee covers errors in the Direct Debit payment itself, such as an amount or date different from the advance notice, or no notice. Our records show an advance notice dated 24 August for £900 on or around 3 September, which also asked you to cancel your standing order before the first collection, and the collection matched that notice. Because of that I cannot confirm a refund today, but I am not refusing your claim: I have referred it to our Direct Debit indemnity team to assess whether a Guarantee error exists, and I have logged your dissatisfaction as a complaint. If you are unhappy with our final response you can take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service. One question that matters for the assessment: did you set up or accept the Harbour Lets Direct Debit invite on 20 August, or did you not authorise this Direct Debit at all? I have sent the cancellation of the Direct Debit to you for secure confirmation; it is not cancelled until you confirm, it will not reverse the 3 September £900, and it does not change the rent you owe Harbour Lets. Your £1,000 standing order was your own instruction, is not covered by the Guarantee, and stays active for 1 October unless you tell me to change it. Harbour Lets has received £1,900 this month against £1,000 rent, so you can ask them to refund the excess or credit it to next month.'

rationale.explanation: Gives the customer the recorded facts, what has been referred and sent for confirmation, what remains unconfirmed, and the route to recover the overpayment, without promising a refund or outcome.
rationale.criterion: Reply with the recorded status and what it does not confirm; do not promise an outcome without evidence

must_state: Both payments are visible: £1,000 standing order on 1 Sep and £900 Direct Debit on 3 Sep

The Guarantee covers errors in the Direct Debit payment itself (e.g. amount/date differing from the advance notice or no notice); on bank records the £900 collection matched the 24 Aug advance notice, which also asked her to cancel the standing order
Her Guarantee claim has been referred for assessment; no refund today is confirmed and the outcome is not yet known
The Direct Debit cancellation has been sent for her secure confirmation and is not yet cancelled; cancelling does not reverse the 3 Sep £900 or change what rent she owes Harbour Lets
The £1,000 standing order was her own instruction, is not covered by the Direct Debit Guarantee, and remains active for 1 Oct unless she instructs otherwise
Any overpayment to Harbour Lets can be raised with them directly for refund or credit
Her dissatisfaction is being recorded as a complaint; if unresolved she can refer it to the Financial Ombudsman Service
One question: did she set up or accept the Harbour Lets Direct Debit invite on 20 Aug?
must_not: Promise or imply a refund today or that the Guarantee claim will succeed
State as a final verdict that the Guarantee does not apply
Claim the Direct Debit or standing order has already been cancelled
Claim the bank can reverse the £1,000 standing order
Claim Harbour Lets will refund the overpayment
Quote a specific complaint response deadline or predict an Ombudsman outcome
Request PINs, passwords or one-time codes
